cases.command: mkdir -p /data/fcE_tr && f=/data/fcE_tr/big; truncate -s 9M $f; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 8388600 $f; printf MARKER >> $f; truncate -s 8388610 $f; printf TAIL >> $f; truncate -s 9M $f; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 8388612 $f; head -c 8388606 $f | tail -c 6; echo; tail -c 2 $f; echo; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 8388603 $f; tail -c 3 $f; echo; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 60000 $f; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 10 $f; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 0 $f; wc -c < $f; rm -rf /data/fcE_tr
cases.note: Sizes either side of drive9's 8 MiB part and 50,000-byte inline threshold. On tidb-filesystem the cut to 8,388,612 bytes falls in the second part, so drive9 copies the first part and MARKER must survive; the cuts to 8,388,603, 60,000 and 10 bytes go through a patch upload of the first part, and the growth goes through a native append.

cases.command: mkdir -p /data/fcE_ts2 && f=/data/fcE_ts2/s; printf 'hello world' > $f; truncate -s 5 $f; cat $f; echo; truncate -s 7 $f; wc -c < $f; tail -c 2 $f | tr '\0' z; echo; truncate -s 0 $f; wc -c < $f; truncate -s 3 /data/fcE_ts2/new; wc -c < /data/fcE_ts2/new; printf abc > $f; : > $f; wc -c < $f; rm -rf /data/fcE_ts2
